items.readable_text:
Content:
To plot the graph of [MATH: y=-2(3^x),] we take the curve [MATH: y=2(3^x)] and reflect it in the [MATH: x]-axis, as shown below:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/2a759a4f9b945d99b51c9f355143fa0e]

Content:
This transformation is called a reflection in the [MATH: \boldsymbol{x}]-axis, and it occurs because the output [MATH: y]-values of the function [MATH: y=2(3^x)] are made negative by the transformation.

Content:
If we combine vertical translations with reflection, we get a general form

Content:
[MATH: y = -a(b^x) + k.]

Content:
This is the equation of a reflected exponential graph [MATH: y=-a(b^x)] that is translated [MATH: k] units up.

sections.normalized_html:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

  • We take the curve [MATH: y=2(7^x).]

  • Reflect it on the [MATH: x]-axis to give [MATH: y=-2(7^x).] The [MATH: y]-intercept moves from [MATH: (0,2)] to [MATH: (0,-2)] but the horizontal asymptote stays at [MATH: y=0.]

  • Then, vertically shift it by [MATH: 1] unit down to give [MATH: y=-2(7^x)-1.] The point [MATH: (0,-2)] moves to [MATH: (0,-3)] and the horizontal asymptote moves from [MATH: y=0] to [MATH: y=-1.]
